_comment: Accepted pnpm-audit exceptions — task-prod-runtime-vulns (2026-08-16/17, round 3 per security-review PR #536); round 4 (2026-09-02, infra/audit-undici-advisories) added the @xmldom/xmldom group below. Read scripts/devops/check-pnpm-audit.mjs's module doc before editing. Every group below is keyed by exact GHSA id (not just a package name) — a NEW advisory id for an already-listed package is NOT covered and will gate CI red until it is triaged and either fixed or added here with its own reason. Every group MUST carry a `reason` of meaningful length (enforced by the guard, not just convention) — an empty or placeholder reason makes the guard treat the whole group as unaccepted regardless of severity. Round 2: vite/postcss/nanoid/@babel/core/js-yaml/qs/brace-expansion were ALL genuinely fixed (not just documented) after security-review found the earlier 'no fix below a major' reasons factually wrong for several of them — dependency bump + `pnpm dedupe`, or a root pnpm.overrides entry, none crossing a version-pins.md pin. Round 3: `esbuild` (round 2's remaining exception) is ALSO genuinely fixed now — a naive blanket `esbuild` override broke `pnpm build` (Vite's OWN internal esbuild@0.25.12 dependency, itself never vulnerable to either GHSA, conflicts with a forced newer version underneath it), but a SELECTOR override scoped to only the two actually-vulnerable consumers (`"tsx>esbuild"`, `"@esbuild-kit/core-utils>esbuild"` in root package.json) resolves both without ever touching Vite's own untouched, unaffected esbuild edge. Round 4: the gate went red again on `main` from FOUR newly-published advisories against packages that already had a pnpm.overrides floor from earlier rounds (qs >=6.15.2, fastify ^5.12.0, fast-uri >=3.1.5) — the floor itself hadn't moved since it was set, but newer CVEs raised the bar above it. All three were genuinely fixed by tightening the existing override floor (qs >=6.16.0, fastify ^5.12.1, fast-uri >=3.1.6 — still inside the ^5.8.5 fastify pin, no pin crossed); a fourth advisory (@xmldom/xmldom) was deliberately NOT fixed the same way at that time (historical; that group no longer exists — see Round 6 at the end). `pnpm --filter @crm/web build` before/after: identical PWA precache (99 entries, 3700.99 KiB) — none of the touched packages reach the shipped SPA bundle. Round 5 (2026-10-02, infra/audit-gate-refresh): gate red again on 28 newly-published advisories. 22 genuinely fixed by version bumps (axios ^1.20.0, @nestjs/platform-fastify ^11.2.4, overrides fastify ^5.12.5 / fast-uri >=3.1.8 / brace-expansion >=5.0.12 — no version-pins.md pin crossed; Fastify stays inside ^5.8.5 line); 6 new undici advisories added to the existing dev-only undici group (jsdom test polyfill, same reachability proof as before). Round 6 (2026-10-22, devops/vitest-audit-advisories): vitest 4.1.11 -> 4.1.12 genuinely fixed GHSA-qxg6-89mg-rqv8 and GHSA-xp26-3454-mjgp (@vitest/mocker); no exception added. The @xmldom/xmldom group (10 GHSA ids) was REMOVED, not carried over: the lockfile resolves @xmldom/xmldom 0.8.15 (patched) via the single apps/api -> mammoth edge (pnpm why @xmldom/xmldom -r) and pnpm audit reports none of those ids. The removed group justified itself with a claim that bumping to 0.8.15 would break resume-text-extraction.service.spec.ts; that claim was STALE — the spec was already rebuilt for 0.8.15 and passes (checked 2026-10-22). A stale justification keeps a dead exception alive, so re-verify any reason before copying it forward. Round 7 (2026-10-24, fix/zod-advisory-ghsa-mrhx): zod 4.6.5 -> 4.6.7 genuinely fixed GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5 (<4.6.6) in all manifests (still inside the v4 pin); no exception added. The braces (GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm) and sprintf-js (GHSA-hp3w-g68c-fv3c) groups were REMOVED: pnpm audit no longer reports either id (checked 2026-10-24 with node scripts/devops/check-pnpm-audit.mjs), so their reachability reasons had nothing left to justify. The exceptions list is now empty; a new advisory for either package gates CI until it is triaged afresh.

exceptions.reason: `minimatch` is installed on three major lines (3.1.5, 5.1.9, 10.2.5) and the advisory's patched range is >=11.0.1, so EVERY fix crosses a major boundary for every consumer; no in-major patch exists (latest is 11.0.3; the 3.x/5.x/10.x lines are unpatched), so a bounded override is not possible (runbook Step 2). Forcing 11.x under glob 11/13 (which declare minimatch ^10), @nestjs/cli's fork-ts-checker-webpack-plugin (^3) and jake -> filelist (^5) would run those tools against an API they were not built for, untested. Verified with `pnpm why minimatch -r` (2026-10-31): zero paths under a plain `dependencies:` heading in any workspace package (api, web, landing, e2e, shared, inference); every path is under `devDependencies:`. Consumers seen: @lingui/cli -> glob, @nestjs/cli -> glob / fork-ts-checker-webpack-plugin (3.1.5), vite-plugin-pwa -> workbox-build -> glob / ejs -> jake -> filelist (5.1.9), plus other build-tool chains on 10.2.5: the Lingui message-extraction CLI, the Nest build CLI, the PWA build step and lint/format tooling; none is bundled into the shipped SPA or loaded by the API runtime. GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249 is a denial of service through globparts amplification when minimatch compiles an attacker-supplied glob PATTERN; the patterns these tools feed it come from our own committed config and repository file names, never from request data or other untrusted input, so the worst outcome is a slow or stuck local/CI dev command. Deferred until the consumers (glob, @nestjs/cli, workbox-build, jake) ship versions on minimatch >=11; re-check by 2026-12-01 or on any new advisory, then add an override floor.

`glob` is installed as 11.1.0 (@lingui/cli, workbox-build via vite-plugin-pwa) and 13.0.6 (@nestjs/cli); the advisory's vulnerable range is >=9.0.0 <=14.0.1 and the patched range is >=14.0.2, so the fix is a major bump (11 -> 14, 13 -> 14) for both consumers with no in-major patch (runbook Step 2); an override would force an API those tools never tested against, and Step 3's silent-green risk applies to build tooling we have no spec for. Verified with `pnpm why glob -r` (2026-10-31): zero paths under a plain `dependencies:` heading in any workspace package (api, web, landing, e2e, shared, inference); every path is under `devDependencies:`. Paths: root and apps/web @lingui/cli (and @lingui/vite-plugin -> @lingui/cli) -> glob 11.1.0, apps/web vite-plugin-pwa -> workbox-build -> glob 11.1.0, apps/api @nestjs/cli -> glob 13.0.6: the Lingui extraction CLI, the PWA service-worker build and the Nest build CLI, never bundled into the SPA nor loaded by the API runtime. GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4 is an AbortSignal cancellation bypass: filesystem traversal continues after a caller-supplied signal aborts or times out; these tools run glob over our own repository tree to completion (no untrusted pattern, no abort/timeout path on a request), so the worst outcome is a local/CI build command doing extra directory walking. Deferred until @lingui/cli, workbox-build and @nestjs/cli ship versions on glob >=14.0.2; re-check by 2026-12-01 or on any new advisory, then add an override floor.
